correctness.rationale: The 2n supporting facets are explicit, and a direction illuminates a vertex iff all incident facet forms are strictly negative. For equal pole heights, the maximum projection bound max_j<w_j,s>≥cos(π/n)||s|| forces |z|>h||s|| for pole illumination; averaging adjacent equatorial inequalities forces |z|<h||s|| for any equatorial illumination. Thus all pole directions are disjoint from equator directions. Planar equiangular spacing gives exact capacity m=floor((n-1)/2), realized by every consecutive m-block. Two poles force two units plus n/m fractional or ceil(n/m) ordinary. Tight incidence and a cyclic linear recurrence give the complete aggregate fractional optimizers. For the unequal pentagonal witness the 5 explicit vectors (-w_j,-11/10) illuminate the upper apex and neighboring pairs, certified by the exact positive-radical comparison 19sqrt(5)>41. The lower apex still cannot share with any equatorial vertex; equatorial capacity two yields lower bounds 1+5/2 and ceil(7/2), attained by the explicit vectors. Standalone verify.py checks finite analogues; it is supplementary rather than the proof.

value.rationale: The strict pole/equator lemma is structural across unbounded regular bipyramid orders and all positive equal heights. The result classifies both ordinary and fractional illumination and the complete fractional optimizer face, with a sharp mod-four change in optimizer freedom. Most significantly, an explicit same-combinatorial-type unequal-height pentagonal bipyramid strictly drops the two invariants from 5 and 9/2 to 4 and 7/2; hence symmetric free-sum additivity cannot be extended to arbitrary asymmetric double-pyramid geometry. These properties address the relationship of join geometry, integrality gaps and illumination rigidity, beyond a routine finite table.
